None of this should be reduced to speculative theory simply because the
Council has not adjudicated it. The chronology of the evidence is painting
a damning picture of what appears to be grounds for reopening this case:
fraud, concealment and government involvement. These are matters I am
investigating, and I encourage everyone involved to conduct their own
research and investigation.


Before returning to the formal substance of this communication, I want to
speak plainly and personally. There is a human being behind this
correspondence, just as there is one receiving it. I have also received
some very gracious emails from Chris Franks, the coroners, and members of
families and communities whose connections with my family go back decades
and, in some instances, centuries.


First, I reject what I regard as a coercive, hostage-like relationship with
the local authorities. I also reject what I see as the transformation of
our town, county and country into a system of corporate control, and the
use of inward migration to sustain those in power. These are serious
political objections, not casual remarks. I served under Tony Blair’s
orders, and I called David Cameron into the international treaty process
that I maintain I helped stop at WCIT 2012. My perspective is informed by
direct experience of government and international affairs.


What happened to our stronghold, and the destruction of our ancient
history, heritage and family life, is, in my view, tantamount to ethnic
cleansing. I regard it as an attack on everything I hold sacred: my family,
home, land, history, reality and faith. The situation was untenable then.
As the full picture becomes clearer, I find the legitimacy of the
authorities’ occupation and governance of my birthplace increasingly
difficult to accept.


If this has all been a profound misunderstanding, and nobody is responsible
for wrongdoing, then that needs to be demonstrated through evidence and
clear answers. So far, I have received little reassurance from any of you
that my interpretation is mistaken.


I acknowledge my own misunderstandings. I understood that you had already
retired, which was incorrect. Until recently, I also believed the 1987
merger of parcels had occurred in 1983. This is a complex case, and I do
not claim to understand every aspect of it. Resolving it will require a
collective effort. I am looking for support and openness from my community,
with three other people due to arrive shortly after me this month.


Legitimacy is the only basis on which I will recognise authority here. Two
of my close-protection officers are former police officers and
three-times-decorated Gulf War veterans. I have shared this matter with
them. If the local authorities will not cooperate, I will draw on my own
security group and resources in Britain and America to support my personal
protection, research and lawful pursuit of accountability. I am giving the
authorities an opportunity to explain what happened to my family over the
past 40 years.


As you may be able to tell, I have largely lost confidence that the system
operating here is democratic or lawful. I regard the British State’s
conduct towards my family as terroristic. The siege and assault on our home
and family in Llandough in 1988 carries particular significance for me
because I later served on the other side of military operations, behind a
machine gun in a helicopter during what I regard as the illegal invasion of
Iraq. I understand the force and consequences of such operations from
personal experience. That history informs the seriousness of my position;
it is not a threat.


My return to Cardiff last month brought back memories of a military tour in
the Middle East in 2005, when two SAS personnel were held by Iraqi police
and, as I understood the situation, faced imminent execution. We had to
break through the prison walls to get them out. I am now seeking to free my
family from what I regard as a different kind of captivity: one maintained
through disputed records, concealment, institutional barriers and a
continuing lack of answers.


The walls in this case are not physical. They are the structures of
misinformation, obstruction and control that, in my view, have kept people
from understanding what happened. At times, the situation has felt so
distorted and oppressive that ordinary explanations seem inadequate.


If this case is not properly addressed, I believe the consequences for the
village and the institutions involved could be profound. This is not a
small matter. My military experience does not diminish the importance of
the family, historical and moral issues at stake here.


Nor can everyone involved continue to claim ignorance of the information
now being brought forward. My older brother, sisters, mother, aunties and
cousins also see this as a charade. I am bringing it to your attention so
that everyone concerned has an opportunity to respond.


So far, I have encountered barriers, delays, paywalls and excuses. You
kindly directed us to material such as the 1939 agreement, which excludes
our parcel. I acknowledge that assistance. However, your initial response
was that you were unwilling to become involved, and that remains part of
the history of this correspondence.


Please understand that I bring this matter to the local authorities—whose
legitimacy in this case I dispute—after considerable personal trauma,
misinformation, fragmented information and expense. I attended private
boarding school, and my career began in military intelligence, but the
events of 1988 nevertheless pushed our family into a fundamentally
different life.


More recently, I left my wife and daughter at our villa in the Caribbean
and spent the past year in a cabin in southern Argentina, trying to
understand this case. The time and strain involved have contributed to the
breakdown of my marriage and another family separation. While
correspondence continues to be delayed for months, those personal
consequences are real and ongoing. Each dismissal or inadequate response
adds to them.


I am a military professional, and I am committed to understanding what
happened. That is why I flew 7,000 miles to seek answers in person. If this
is my family’s land, how did others come to occupy it? I remain unconvinced
by the explanations being provided.


Those explanations may have gone unchallenged when I was an infant, my
mother was pregnant and my father was terminally ill. But my grandmother,
Mary Williams—a disabled, widowed pensioner—had seven children, who in turn
had children of their own. Our family has grown considerably, and many of
us now want answers.


I also have more than 50 former soldiers in my US-based private security
group, with a satellite office here. I mention this to explain the
resources and support available to me, not to suggest that this dispute
should be resolved through force. My family’s determination to establish
the truth extends well beyond me.


I am no longer based here. I have reached the conclusion that the British
State is engaged in the ethnic cleansing of Welsh nationals in Wales. That
is part of why I am now based in Patagonia, Argentina, where our Welsh
history and heritage are celebrated, and where I am pursuing legal
personhood arrangements for my AI agents.


My purpose here is to bring the evidence into the open and initiate
accountability. The authorities will then have to address the concerns of
the wider family and others affected. I am gathering evidence partly for
the replica of Great House Farm that I am constructing in Patagonia as a
museum and third home. If that process establishes fraud, concealment and
government involvement, I will pursue the reopening of the case.


[https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate](
https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate)


My wife, from whom I am separating, and I will not allow our daughter,
whose birth is unregistered, to set foot in Wales unless it is decolonised
or the present British establishment and system of government are replaced.


I also exported my dog from our livery yard in Monknash in 2024 following
an incident in which, according to my account, an Afghan migrant entered
our horse yard and indoor riding school and attempted to steal him. I
believed the intention was to eat him.


My first child was abducted at 36 days old in 2013, and I have not seen
that child since. Experiences such as these have left me with a profound
sense that the institutions operating here are failing to protect my
family. At times, that experience has felt almost demonic in its cruelty
and incomprehensibility.


My business associates, former soldiers and family members are gathering
around this matter, with some travelling into the region, because they
understand its potential significance. If my interpretation of this case
and the alleged corruption within the local authorities is correct, the
implications may extend beyond one family’s property dispute and into the
wider land market.


I am not suggesting that those broader implications alone establish the
threshold for reopening this case. I am saying that ours may be one of the
earliest—possibly the first—of a series of parallel cases nationwide.


I see a potential parallel with Cyprus, where I served as guard commander
at RAF Akrotiri. My understanding of the situation there involved the
United Nations in Nicosia and questions of returning land to its original
inhabitants after decades of occupation, or providing reparations. That
experience informs how I view the possibilities here.


Decolonisation is not merely political or figurative, Paul. It concerns
land, ownership, restitution and practical implementation. I believe those
issues will become increasingly apparent through this case and others now
emerging nationwide.


Having recently worked on establishing the car-finance compensation claims
scheme and its information systems, against the background of the FCA’s
work and last year’s court rulings, I see a further parallel. Individual
cases can expose wider patterns and lead to scrutiny of an entire system.
As cases resembling my family’s experience in Llandough emerge nationally
and internationally, that possibility deserves serious attention.


Do you see the parallel? The websites below illustrate the comparison I am
drawing. In my view, neither underlying system should be able to continue
functioning as it does without scrutiny and accountability.

https://car.financecheque.uk

https://bucklerfamily.estate


... but I digress. To continue from my earlier point I'm not asking
Llandough Community Council to adjudicate title or pronounce upon matters
outside its legal remit. The Council’s institutional authority is not
itself proof of the legitimacy of a title position. Its responsibility is
to account accurately for its own records, knowledge, representations,
decisions and referrals, and to disclose the recorded information it holds.

The question of legitimacy must be assessed against the underlying
documents and relevant legal acts, rather than presumed from administrative
status or the repetition of an earlier account. I expect the Council to
distinguish primary documentary evidence, recorded statements, family
evidence and inference when dealing with these matters.
2. Formal request for internal review — refusal dated 11 October 2026

Please treat this section as my formal request for an internal review of
the refusal of my original request submitted on 21 September 2026.

That request covered:

   1. Records created after 2002 concerning Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr,
   Church View Close, the green—including references to VG41—and the roadside
   verge beside the churchyard wall.
   2. Photographs, postcards and other images, of any date, depicting the
   farmhouse, farm buildings, green or surrounding church area.
   3. Records concerning material transferred from Penarth Town Council
   during the 1982 local-government reorganisation, and information held by
   the Council about the whereabouts or deposit of earlier Llandough community
   records.

Your refusal explains that searching minutes and related documentation
across a period of approximately 2002–2016 would exceed the appropriate
cost limit. It refers to 224 sets of records and estimates 20 minutes to
read each set and a further 10 minutes to assess it, but gives a total of
2,240 minutes, or approximately 37 hours.

Those figures are internally inconsistent. At 30 minutes per set, 224 sets
would amount to 6,720 minutes, or 112 hours. The stated 2,240 minutes
equates to 10 minutes per set. More importantly, the response does not
explain precisely which activities have been included in the estimate.

Please have the reviewer consider the following matters:

   - How the estimate was calculated, including the number and nature of
   the records assumed to require examination.
   - Whether the estimate was applied to every part of the request,
   including photographic material and records concerning the 1982 transfer,
   rather than treating all categories as if they required the same search.
   - Whether existing indexes, catalogues, minute headings, document
   descriptions, filing systems or other finding aids permit targeted searches
   before individual records are examined.
   - Whether a targeted search using the place names, former names, dates
   and subjects identified in my request could provide a materially less
   costly route to the information.
   - Whether the requested environmental information must be considered
   under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004, rather than being
   refused solely by reference to the Freedom of Information Act cost limit.

Please identify how the stated 20 minutes for reading and 10 minutes for
assessment per set correspond to the permitted activities under regulation
4(3) of the Freedom of Information and Data Protection (Appropriate Limit
and Fees) Regulations 2004. In particular, distinguish time spent
determining whether the requested information is held, locating, retrieving
or extracting it from time spent on activities that cannot lawfully be
included in the section 12 estimate.

If the Council relies on regulation 12(4)(b) of the Environmental
Information Regulations, please identify that exception expressly, provide
the relevant reasoning and carry out the required public-interest
assessment, including the presumption in favour of disclosure. Do not treat
the FOIA section 12 estimate as a substitute for determining which legal
regime applies to each category.

Please also address the duty to provide reasonable advice and assistance
under section 16 FOIA and, where applicable, regulation 9 of the
Environmental Information Regulations. Your suggestion that I narrow the
date range to 2002–2006 is noted, but I ask the reviewer to consider what
targeted searches or available indexes could reasonably be used to address
the original request before concluding that the information cannot be
provided.

Please confirm receipt of this internal review request, identify who will
conduct the review, and provide the anticipated response date. Where
reasonably practicable, the review should be undertaken by someone
independent of the original refusal.
3. Further request for recorded information — 1986–1990 and associated land
matters

In addition to the original request, please treat this section as a new
request for recorded information under FOIA and, where applicable, the
Environmental Information Regulations. It is directed to records held by
the Council and does not presume that any particular document exists.

*A. Great House Farm: occupation, title, development and demolition*

Please disclose minutes, agendas, reports, correspondence, letters, notes,
complaints, representations, referrals and other recorded information
created between 1 January 1986 and 31 December 1990 concerning Great House
Farm / Tŷ Mawr, including its occupation, title, tenure, proposed
development, removal of the occupants or demolition of the farmhouse and
associated buildings.

This includes records of communications with Vale of Glamorgan Council,
planning authorities, developers, solicitors, landowners, police, heritage
bodies or other public authorities concerning those subjects.

Please include any records containing statements attributed to my late
father, William “Billy” Buckler, about the property, occupation, title or
alleged fraud. References to alleged fraud identify a subject for the
search; they are not a claim that a Council record or finding establishing
fraud necessarily exists.

*B. Planning records and annexes*

Please identify and disclose the Council-held planning records, plans,
supporting documents, annexes, correspondence and associated material
relating to application 89/01396/OUT and any related consideration of the
redevelopment of the site.

I have been unable to locate certain associated annexes in my copy. Please
confirm whether the Council holds them and, if not, whether its records
identify another custodian or archive.

*C. Green, verge, trees and woodland*

Please disclose records held by the Council concerning the history, status,
boundaries, maintenance, planting, ownership representations or public use
of the green, the roadside verge beside the churchyard wall, and the
woodland associated with the former farm.

This includes relevant correspondence, complaints, maps, plans, site-visit
records, referrals and communications with landowners, residents,
charities, the Vale of Glamorgan Council or other responsible bodies.

I have also received information raising a concern that some gardens at
Church View Close may extend beyond their recorded boundaries into
adjoining woodland. I identify this as an unverified concern requiring
documentary clarification, not as an established finding of encroachment or
wrongdoing. Please disclose any Council-held records relating to the
boundaries, complaints or enquiries about this area.

I recognise that the official VG41 registration file is understood to be
held by the Vale of Glamorgan Council. I am requesting records held by
Llandough Community Council, including any copies, correspondence,
representations or referrals concerning the green or its registration—not
suggesting that this Council is the custodian of another authority’s file.

Please search relevant paper and electronic records, including
correspondence and records held in archived or transferred collections that
remain accessible to the Council. If any part of this request is considered
too broad, please identify the specific part and explain what narrower
search is practicable. If records are not held, please say so and identify
any known transfer or deposit location where possible.
4. Subject access request — my personal data

Separately, I make a subject access request under Article 15 of the UK GDPR
and the Data Protection Act 2018 for personal data about me, Sion Buckler,
held by the Council.

The request covers personal data concerning my childhood association with
Great House Farm, the events surrounding the removal of my family from the
farmhouse and its demolition in 1988, and subsequent Council records
referring to me or recording information about me in connection with these
events.

Please search relevant Council-held correspondence, minutes, reports,
notes, referrals, photographs and other records, whether paper or
electronic. This request concerns my personal data; it is not a request for
unrestricted disclosure of every record concerning my late father or the
property.

Please acknowledge this as a subject access request and deal with it under
the applicable data-protection procedure. If you require proportionate
identification information to verify my identity, please specify what is
required.
5. Matters said to be for the “October meeting”

Your email of 11 October states that other matters raised in my
correspondence “will be considered at the October meeting of the council”
and that you will provide the Council’s views afterwards.

Please confirm whether that meeting has already taken place.

If it has, please provide the exact date, the relevant agenda and papers,
the minute or other formal record of consideration, and any decision or
action arising in relation to the matters I raised.

If it has not yet taken place, please provide the confirmed date, time,
venue and public-access arrangements, together with the draft or published
agenda showing which of my matters are scheduled for consideration.

Those matters include:

   - The Council’s historic knowledge of Great House Farm, its surroundings
   and the green, and any representations or records it holds concerning these
   matters.
   - The available documentary and photographic record relating to the site
   and its redevelopment.
   - The concerns raised about the adjoining woodland and garden
   boundaries, insofar as they fall within the Council’s records or remit.
   - The availability of the relevant planning annexes and the location of
   any missing records.
   - Whether the Council would consider a suitable historical
   interpretation or memorial for the former farmhouse and its significance to
   the local community.

I also repeat my request that the Council pass my contact details to any
former councillor, clerk or local resident who is willing to contact me
about relevant historical knowledge. I am not asking the Council to
disclose those individuals’ personal contact details without their consent.

I remain willing to give a short presentation on the documentary record at
no charge if the Council considers that useful. Please record the offer and
advise whether it will be considered.

If the meeting is open to the public, please also advise how a member of
the public may make representations on relevant business, having regard to
section 48 of the Local Government and Elections (Wales) Act 2021 and the
Council’s meeting arrangements.

If the Council does not provide these particulars or identify the relevant
published notice, please explain the basis on which I am expected to verify
that the promised consideration has occurred or will occur. I will retain
the omission and any subsequent response as part of the record of the
Council’s handling of these matters.
6. Clerk’s appointment and responsibility for records

For completeness, I ask for clarification of the present clerking and
records arrangements because they bear directly on the identification,
custody and review of the records requested.

I have seen public references to your retirement from a separate role with
One Voice Wales in 2026, earlier references in 2021 to possible retirement
from Llandough Community Council, and subsequent discussion about whether
the Council had a clerk. I do not treat those references or social-media
comments as verified facts, and I draw no adverse inference from them. I
raise the matter openly because responsibility for the Council’s records
and for reviewing the refusal should be clear.

Please confirm:

   - Whether you currently hold the appointment of Clerk to Llandough
   Community Council and act as its Proper Officer.
   - Whether any change of appointment, acting arrangement or transfer of
   responsibility has affected the custody or management of the relevant
   records.
   - Who is currently responsible for the Council’s records and who will
   conduct the internal review.

7. Charges and response

I have not authorised any discretionary paid search. Please do not treat
this email as agreement to incur a charge. If you consider that any part of
the request may lawfully attract a fee, please identify the legal basis,
the precise work proposed and the amount in writing before proceeding on
that basis.

Please acknowledge each procedural element of this email, distinguish the
internal review from the further information request and subject access
request, and identify any part you consider cannot be processed as
submitted, together with the reason and the available remedy.

I expect the Council’s response to address the recorded evidence and the
applicable obligations directly. I am not asking the Council to endorse my
conclusions merely because I advance them; I am asking it to disclose and
account for the records within its custody and to distinguish what the
records establish from what remains uncertain.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

Dear Sion Buckler,

Thank you for your email.

UPDATE: FIREWORKS
RESPONSE FROM POLICE AND COUNCIL


**
------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Hywel

Fireworks continue to cause unacceptable noise disturbances in our community.

I raised the issue at Full Council on Monday, emphasising the importance of both the Council and the Police working together.

You can watch my comments here.  (https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1JExrTZK3w/)

https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1JExrTZK3w/

On Wednesday, our village experienced another incident.

It is clear neither the police nor the Vale of Glamorgan Council have taken sufficient action to date to address this problem.

Both authorities have failed to fulfill their duties to protect our community.

I've written to both authorities to raise serious concerns.

You can read my letter below.
FAO: South Wales Police
Vale of Glamorgan Council

8th October 2026


Dear both

Illegal firework usage in Llandough

I’m saddened to report that another firework related incident took place in Llandough last night.

This is impacting some of the most vulnerable members of our community, causing distress to the elderly, small children and animals.

It is apparent that those responsible for setting off fireworks are not residents and instead come into the community from outside.

A lack of action to date is sending a message to those responsible that their behaviour is acceptable and will be tolerated.

There have been several instances in which fireworks have been set off past 11.00pm at night, in direct contravention of the law. There may also be other laws and regulations that have been broken.

I would therefore be grateful if you would:

- Outline full details of all firework-related incidents in the Llandough ward reported to your respective authorities within the past 24 months;

- Confirm all actions that were taken following those incidents to address the problems reported;

- Outline all actions proposed by your authorities to prevent inappropriate firework usage in the Llandough ward in future;

- Confirm all measures available to your respective authorities to detain and apprehend the individuals responsible for inappropriate firework usage in the Community of Llandough as well as any restrictions that may be imposed to prohibit those individuals from entering the Community boundary; and

- Confirm details of any powers conferred on your respective authorities which enable you to introduce additional regulations or byelaws to impose stricter restrictions prohibiting firework usage within the Community of Llandough.

I have not copied this message to our PSCOs because they are not responsible for operational decisions, and as such it would be unfair to attribute blame to them for the failure to address this problem.

However, I reiterate my request for your respective authorities to meet with me at the earliest convenience to discuss this ongoing problem, with an invitation also extended to our PCSOs.

Thank you for your consideration of this matter, and I look forward to your prompt response.

Kind regards,

Cllr George Carroll
Elected member

Llandough ward
Vale of Glamorgan Council
I'm pleased to report both authorities responded promptly.

The Police have confirmed a Problem Oriented Police Plan is being developed in conjunction with our PCSOs.

The Inspector has confirmed he'll update me in due course, with further escalation promised if this proves insufficient.

The Council too have agreed to take part in a multi-agency meeting to address the problem.

The time for discussion has long passed.

We need to see surveillance and enforcement, so that those responsible for these disturbances know their behaviour will not be tolerated.

As a community, it's vital we keep up the pressure.


**
------------------------------------------------------------

Dear Mr Buckler,

Many thanks for your e-mail below and your request for Scrutiny to consider the topic suggested as part of it's Task and Finish work.

Unfortunately, on this occasion we will be unable to consider the request for several reasons:

1. The purpose of Task and Finish is to review existing policy Council considerations and identify areas for future policy direction at a strategic level impacting on a county wide basis. These topics are purposefully strategic in manner, and are based upon areas that Committees determine to have the most positive impact.

2. In addition to the above, the purpose of Scrutiny is not to review evidence related to individual historical decisions and make subsequent recommendations, particularly related to planning, which should be navigated through other channels.

3. We are aware through other correspondence to which you have copied us into that there are ongoing concerns being raised through a variety of channels including Welsh Government, CADW, MSs and MPs, and as such it would not be appropriate for a Scrutiny Task and Finish to add an additional layer of stakeholders and complexity in exploring the issues; notwithstanding points 1 and 2 raised.

Kind Regards,
James

Dear Mr Buckler,

Thank you for your email of  21 September 2026 making a request for 
information.

We are treating your correspondence as a request for information under 
the Freedom of Information Act 2000 (the act).

Under the provisions of the act and as defined by "The Freedom of 
Information and Data Protection (Appropriate Limit and Fees) Regulations 
2004" (the regulations) , an authority is not obliged to comply with a 
request for information if the authority estimates that the cost of 
complying with the request would exceed the "appropriate limit".  This 
appropriate limit is set by the regulations at £450 for our type of 
authority.

In the regulations our staff time is valued at £25 per hour.  This has 
the effect of imposing a time limit of 18 hours of staff time for 
activities specified in the regulations.

  The regulations make the following activities by an authority countable 
towards the cost limit.

  	* determining whether it holds the information,

  	* locating the information, or a document which may contain the 
information,

  	* retrieving the information, or a document which may contain the 
information, and

  	* extracting the information from a document containing it.

  We have estimated the time and therefore costs as provided by the 
regulations, and in doing so have taken into account the above 
activities.

  We estimate that this work will take in excess of 18 hours of effort by 
our staff. As we have a significant amount of documents on file from the 
period 2002-2016 where minutes are in documents rather than published on 
the website or in archives.

  We estimate this will exceed the limit provided for by the regulations 
and therefore your request is refused on the grounds provided for under 
section 12 of the act.

Our estimate of time is based on the requirement to search all minutes 
of the council and its committees for a period of 14 years. It is 
estimated that it will take about 20 minutes to read each set of minutes 
of which there are estimated to 224 sets of minutes. It is considered 
that this is likely to take about 10 minutes to assess each set of 
minutes a total of over 2240 minutes which equates to 37 hours.

  We may may be able to provide some information if you are able to 
reduce or refine your request to bring the cost of compliance under the 
regulations limit.  We suggest that you could limit the time frame of 
minutes that we would need to look through. For example 2002-2006.

  Please contact us if you would like to refine your request.

  If you are not satisfied with this response or you wish to complain 
about any aspect of the handling of your request, then you should 
contact us in the first instance and we will undertake an internal 
review.

  If after the internal review you wish to complain further then you can 
complain to the Information Commissioners Office http://www.ico.gov.uk 
[1] and request a decision notice.

The other matters you include in your email will be considered at the 
October meeting of the council and I will let you have the views of the 
council after the meeting.

Dear ITV Viewers Requests,

I am researching the events surrounding Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy’s Church, Cardiff (approx. ST 168 733). Demolition of the farmhouse reportedly began on 6 December 1988. I already hold a partial clip and am trying to identify the complete surviving ITV news item/programme and any associated production record.

Please search, or advise how best to search, ITV’s archive for regional or national news coverage filmed or transmitted in late November and December 1988 concerning Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, farmhouse possession/demolition, or the adjoining site. Relevant records may be indexed by the demolition, local authority, land dispute or reporter rather than the farm name.

If a match is found, please provide:
1. programme/news-item title, transmission date/time, regional service and archive reference;
2. whether a complete transmitted segment, original camera footage/rushes, outtakes, narration/script, running order, transmission log or production correspondence survives;
3. available duration/format and whether a viewing or research copy can be supplied;
4. cost, lead time, rights/licensing terms and any limits on personal research use; and
5. if no match is found, the index searched and any alternative archive or successor custodian you recommend.

I am not asking for a determination of title or permission to republish without the appropriate rights. I am seeking to identify and preserve the source record for personal historical research, and can provide the partial clip’s details if that will assist the search.

Thank you for your help.

Yours faithfully,

Dear South Wales Police Information Rights Team,

Please treat this as a request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 for recorded information, excluding personal data and excluding any material for which the appropriate handling route is the separate subject-access request already open. The site is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy’s Church, Cardiff (approx. ST 168 733), and the period is 1 November to 31 December 1988 inclusive.

Please search the relevant South Wales Constabulary / predecessor-force and successor holdings, including any transferred records available to the Force, for existing non-personal records that refer to the site or the events associated with its possession and demolition. Relevant record types, if held, include:
1. incident or occurrence logs and control-room records;
2. deployment, duty or operational logs and any record identifying whether officers attended;
3. correspondence between police, the local authority, landowner/developer, court enforcement officers or other public bodies about the site;
4. any recorded liaison or request for police assistance connected with possession, eviction, demolition, public order or the handling of complaints; and
5. records-transfer, retention or disposal entries for the relevant operational record series, if the responsive records are no longer held.

I am not asserting that a police deployment or a particular incident record necessarily exists. If no responsive record is located, please state that result and identify, so far as reasonably practicable, the record systems, index/series, date range and site/name variants searched. Please distinguish “not found in the systems searched” from a contemporaneous record showing that a file was destroyed or transferred. If transferred, please identify the receiving repository and reference where recorded. If any information is withheld, identify the specific statutory basis and release reasonably separable non-exempt information.

The existing SAR and internal review under ref. 719/26 are separate processes. If a record contains personal data, please do not disclose it through this FOI route; please identify it only as necessary to explain the FOIA decision and continue to handle personal data through the live SAR. This FOI request is not asking South Wales Police to determine ownership or to decide whether an offence occurred.

Please confirm receipt, the request reference, and the statutory response date.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

Dear Cardiff Central Library Local Studies / Manuscripts Team,

Glamorgan Archives has advised me (email reference 2026/4097b, received 30 September 2026) that your library holds a Bute collection containing reference Bute X.6(12), described as “abstracts of payments and receipts by the trustees of the Marquis of Bute’s properties, 1877 (copy)”. I am writing to establish access to that exact item and to ask whether related Bute Estate records in the same collection may assist a targeted historical search.

The property under investigation is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy’s Church (approx. ST 168 733), Cardiff. Please keep this distinct from the separate Llandough Farm opposite the hospital, Llandough juxta-Cowbridge, and Llandow. The historical question is whether surviving estate material in 1876–1878 records a transaction involving Daniel Thomas / D. Thomas and the Bute Estate or its trustees concerning this particular farm/defined parcel. That is a research question, not an assertion that X.6(12) necessarily concerns this property.

Please confirm:
1. whether Bute X.6(12) is still held by Cardiff Central Library, its full item title/date coverage and any catalogue or manuscript identifier;
2. whether the item can be inspected or copied, what the booking/form/fee conditions are, and whether a digital image of the relevant 1877 entry can be supplied;
3. whether staff can check the entry/index for Daniel Thomas, D. Thomas, Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, Llandough Limeworks, quarrying/mineral rights or a dwelling adjoining St Dochdwy’s churchyard;
4. whether related Bute X.6 account/receipt volumes, estate ledgers, correspondence, rent/lease records, conveyances or attached maps/plans survive for 1876–1878 and can be searched; and
5. if no relevant entry is found, which volumes/indexes were checked and whether there is a reliable route to other Cardiff Library manuscript registers or a transfer/custody record.

For any possible match, please provide the exact reference, date, parties as written, property description, amounts/transaction terms if recorded, acreage/boundaries, and whether a map or plan accompanies the entry. Please do not infer that a generic “Llandough” entry refers to this farm without a supporting description.

Thank you for your help. Please direct me to the correct collection custodian if Bute X.6(12) has moved or is managed elsewhere.

Kind regards,
Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

Dear Independent Complaints Reviewer,

Reference ICR/090/26.

I hold the stage-one decision of 19 April 2026 and the stage-two decision of 25 May 2026. I also hold the schedule of 43 documents on the first-registration files released on 30 July 2026.

The family’s established case, recorded on the public wiki and under investigation, is that the 1877 arrangement took effect in 1928, transferring the full Parcel A (house and buildings, barn, stable and west-side yard, garden, northern forest and the south-east ground later registered as VG41) to the Williams family. The 1939 agreement/plan depicts Parcel B only. On the family account, the 1949 attempt to make the occupation of Parcel A permissive failed, title papers were reported missing in 1950–52, and Western Ground Rents’ 4 July 1955 enforcement of Parcel B also seized the Parcel-A forest and green under “whole farm” wording. Later documentary work is directed at corroborating or precisely mapping that account and tracing those areas into later titles.

Four specific points remain unanswered and are relevant to that investigation:

1. The 1969 root deed recited as the root of title does not appear on the schedule. Please confirm whether HMLR holds that deed under any other reference, or whether it was never lodged.
2. What evidence exists on the file of notice or opportunity to object given to the occupying family (Williams / Buckler) in 1982–83.
3. The precise legal and administrative basis for the 1987 title amalgamation that took place while the Court of Appeal proceedings in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler were still live.
4. Whether the inclusion of the woodland (or any land beyond the 1938 conveyance) is regarded as a possible mistake capable of alteration or indemnity under the Land Registration Act 2002 and Practice Guide 39.

Please confirm these points form part of the live investigation and state the exact start date of the ICR six-month period (so that the ~25 November 2026 outer limit can be verified).

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

FORMAL PRESERVATION NOTICE
Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth
Titles: WA231076, WA240304, WA513690 and WA735527
Planning references: 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES

URL: greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com<http://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/>

To each recipient separately, in your own capacity as a current or potential holder, custodian or controller of relevant records:

This notice is addressed to each recipient individually. It is not a joint request, and it does not ask any recipient to speak for, investigate on behalf of, or answer in place of any other person or organisation. Each recipient is asked to respond only in respect of records within that recipient's own possession, custody or control, including records inherited from a predecessor organisation or retained on its behalf.

1. Nature and purpose of this notice

This is a formal preservation notice concerning documentary material relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy's, and the subsequent development of the site, including the area now associated with Church View Close.

It is not a claim form, is not service of proceedings, and is not intended to constitute or replace any FOI request, internal review, complaint, subject-access request or other statutory process already made to any recipient.

The purpose of this notice is to require the preservation of potentially relevant material while the documentary history, title chain, registration history, planning history, possession proceedings, demolition and subsequent development are being reconstructed.

A separate first-stage preservation notice has been issued or is being issued to Cadw / Welsh Government FOI, HM Land Registry Wales Office and DPO, Heneb / GGAT HER, RCAHMW, Vale of Glamorgan FOI Unit and DPO, Glamorgan Archives, South Wales Police FOI, The National Archives, the Wales Office FOI team, and the National Library of Wales. Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd has received a separate preservation letter.

You are receiving this notice separately because the published documentary record places you, or a predecessor whose records may remain in your custody or control, within the documentary, legal, professional, administrative or development chain concerning this land.

2. Land and documentary scope

Please preserve, and do not destroy, alter, overwrite, discard, transfer out of custody without a recorded handover, or otherwise dispose of, any record within your possession, custody or control relating to the land or matters identified below.

The scope includes, without limitation, originals, copies, working papers, drafts, annotations, plans, photographs, negatives, films, tapes, maps, registers, indexes, correspondence, emails and attachments, electronic files, archived mailboxes, databases, metadata, internal notes, meeting records, instructions, client or matter files, survey material and other associated records.

The material requested includes:

1. Historical ownership, occupation and conveyancing

The 1877 split; the 1916 and 1939 tenancies; the 1938 Bute to Western Ground Rents conveyance; the 1969 Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust conveyance; and any plans, schedules, abstracts, searches, correspondence or other documents relied upon in relation to those transactions.

2. Possession proceedings and subsequent litigation

The 1955 High Court and 1962 Cardiff County Court possession orders; the 1974 proceedings; BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2; House of Lords leave papers, including YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536; and Buckler v United Kingdom (1989), including associated correspondence, instructions, evidence, plans and working papers.

3. Land registration

The first registration of WA231076, including the application dated 30 November 1982; the first registration of WA240304, including the application dated 23 February 1983; subsequent amalgamation, transfer or closure; and every plan, conveyance, abstract, search, application, correspondence trail or professional file relied upon in connection with those registrations or changes.

4. 1988 possession and demolition

The taking of possession on or about 29 November 1988 and the demolition commenced on or about 6 December 1988, including any planning, listed-building, heritage, police, enforcement, media, contractor, survey, photographic or inter-agency liaison material.

5. Planning and subsequent development, 1989–1996

Planning application 89/01396/OUT; reserved matters application 92/00671/RES; conditions 16–18; GGAT / Cotswold Archaeology material; records concerning any section 52, section 106, planning obligation, local land charge or equivalent instrument; and the transfer from BP to Ideal Homes dated 3 December 1993, together with all associated plans, correspondence, approvals, agreements, searches and completion material.

6. Family records

Records concerning Mary Doreen Williams (died 1983) and William Buckler, insofar as those records relate to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, the land described above, its occupation, ownership, possession, disposal, registration, development or demolition.

3. Predecessor and inherited files

Where you hold, or may hold, a file originating with a predecessor, successor, merged practice, affiliated practice, client or other entity, that material is also within scope.

This includes, without limitation, records originating from:

Loosemores of Cardiff; Robbins Olivey & Blake Lapthorn / Blake Morgan; Linklaters & Paines; Debenham Tewson / DTZ / Cushman & Wakefield; Wyn Thomas + Partners; Ideal Homes Wales; BP Properties; BP Pension Trust; Cotswold Archaeological Trust; Cardiff Bay Development Corporation; and South Glamorgan County Council.

The reference to a predecessor file does not assert that you necessarily hold such a file. It identifies material for which a reasonable custody or succession inquiry should be made where applicable.

4. Preservation steps

Please take reasonable steps to prevent the routine destruction, deletion, alteration or overwriting of potentially relevant material, including material held in archived mailboxes, legacy systems, off-site storage, document-management systems, backup repositories and other electronic or physical stores.

Where relevant material has been transferred to another repository, archive, successor organisation or third party, please preserve the information necessary to identify the transfer and its current location, including any accession, file, box, reference or custody details.

Nothing in this notice requires the creation of records that do not exist. The request concerns the preservation of records already held or controlled by you.

5. Purpose and legal position

This notice is not a finding against any recipient, and I am not asking any recipient to determine title or adjudicate the underlying dispute.

The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment is relied upon here only for matters actually determined by that judgment, including the issues concerning possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. This preservation notice does not treat that judgment as having determined the complete documentary root of title to the farmhouse parcel.

The underlying documentary history, including the relationship between the farmhouse parcel and the agricultural land subsequently dealt with through Western Ground Rents and BP, remains a matter requiring reconstruction from the primary records.

Accordingly, preservation is requested precisely so that the documentary record can be established from the records themselves rather than through assumptions based on later registration, later occupation, later planning treatment or secondary descriptions.

6. Acknowledgement and identification of records

Please acknowledge receipt of this notice and, in your own capacity, confirm:

(a) the officer, partner, records manager or other person responsible for implementing the preservation hold;

(b) what records within your possession, custody or control you have identified as falling within the scope above; and

(c) where you identify no records within scope, what relevant systems, files, repositories or predecessor records you searched in reaching that conclusion.

A substantive assessment of title is not requested from you. The immediate requirement is preservation and identification of the documentary material you hold.

The public documentary index and developing evidence record is available at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

Please monitor that site for subsequent identification of documents, references and specific schedules relevant to your organisation's records.

Where a reliable public email address is unavailable, a postal preservation notice will also be sent. For example, a postal notice will follow to Loosemores, Alliance House, 18–19 High Street, Cardiff [postcode redacted].

Nothing in this notice constitutes an abandonment, waiver or limitation of any claim, position or remedy concerning title, registration, concealment, limitation, reopening, rectification or alteration of the register, or any associated matter.

FOI Team,

Thank you for the clarification.

Your email of 7 October materially clarifies the position, and I have now corrected my records to distinguish the different Llandough farmsteads.

Ref 13.2 — Llandough Farm opposite the hospital

I understand and accept the distinction in your catalogue description:

“Waterwheel from Llandough Farm (opposite hospital)”

This refers to the separate Llandough Farm in the Llandough near Penarth/Cardiff locality, not to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr. I am not seeking to attribute the waterwheel to Great House Farm.

I will therefore treat Ref 13.2 as a separate Llandough Farm record unless a primary Museum record expressly establishes otherwise.

MS 3360/3 — Great House / Llandough Estate

The more significant clarification is the information you have now supplied from MS 3360/3.

You state that the page records that:

  *   “Great House” formed part of the Llandough Estate sale particulars of 1924;
  *   it was occupied by W.G. Thomas & Sons;
  *   it comprised approximately 202 acres;
  *   it was situated in the Parish of Llanfair; and
  *   the homestead was situated in the Village of Llandough.

Those particulars provide a much more specific identification than the earlier catalogue description.

I am particularly interested in the combination of Llandough Estate + Parish of Llanfair + Village of Llandough + approximately 202 acres + W.G. Thomas & Sons.

Could you therefore confirm one narrow point from the record already examined:

Does the MS 3360/3 page or plan itself contain any further recorded identifier which identifies which historical Llandough is meant — for example the specific place-name form, neighbouring farms, estate owner, parish/benefice wording, acreage breakdown, plan number, tenant information, road, church or other geographical feature?

I am not asking the Museum to make a new identification or to provide an opinion. I am asking only whether such information is actually recorded in the page or plan you have already examined.

There is an important reason for keeping this distinction precise. There are two different farmsteads in the Llandough near Penarth/Cardiff locality relevant to the Museum's records:

  1.  Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, beside St Dochdwy's Church; and
  2.  Llandough Farm, separately described by the Museum as “opposite hospital”.

They must not be treated as alternative names for one farm.

There is also a separate question concerning the Museum's wording “Llandough Church Farm” in the 1858 provenance of accession 63.24. I now understand that this should not automatically be equated with either of the above merely because it contains the word Llandough. Unless the underlying historical evidence expressly identifies the 1858 “Church Farm”, I will continue to record that identity as unresolved.

Filtered schedule

I also accept your clarification that the Museum does not hold a separate recorded audit schedule showing, item by item, which search results staff excluded after reviewing the results.

I therefore do not ask the Museum to create such a schedule.

For the purposes of the record, I will instead distinguish between:

  *   records positively identified as Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr;
  *   records positively identified as the separate Llandough Farm opposite the hospital;
  *   records from other Llandoughs, including Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge;
  *   and source-specific records whose location remains unresolved.

The new MS 3360/3 particulars are sufficiently distinctive to make the underlying page and plan an important identification source, so I would be grateful for confirmation of whether any further geographical identifier is actually recorded there.

Thank you again for the clarification.

Cofion,

Sion Buckler

FIREWORKS: WESTPOINT INDUSTRIAL ESTATE


**
------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Hywel

Thursday night's incident, in which fireworks were set off again at WestPoint Industrial Estate, was completely unacceptable.

People from outside Llandough coming into our community and behaving in such a selfish and inconsiderate manner is becoming an increasing problem.

It shows no regard for the way we do things in Llandough.

We rightly think of others, recognising the impacts our actions can have on some of the most vulnerable members of our community.
Those responsible showed no such regard.

The images above, captured by Peter Griffiths of Vale Sports Arena, demonstrate the extent of the problem.

They show both the number of fireworks set off and the number of people involved.

It also shows authorities must treat stopping this behaviour as a priority.

The noise caused is distressing for many people, including the elderly and those with small children.

It's also distressing for animals, which is a particular problem with Cardiff Dogs Home located within the vicinity.

https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1F4JUgcVux/

I've contacted both South Wales Police and the Vale of Glamorgan Council to request the following things:
* Effective surveillance equipment be installed urgently to identify those responsible;
* Regular nighttime police patrols in the area to stop and apprehend those causing these disturbances;
* Access to the area to be limited to prevent people using it to set off fireworks.

It is a criminal offence to set off fireworks past 11pm at night.

There are also many other laws and regulations that may have been broken.

While Thursday's incident commenced at around 10.30pm, there have been several previous instances in which the law has clearly been breached.

It is punishable by an unlimited fine and up to six months imprisonment.

It is time for the law to be enforced.

Those responsible for causing distress to the vulnerable in Llandough cannot be allowed to think the law does not apply to them.

If you any information about this incident, Hywel, please come forward. It will be treated in the utmost confidence.


**
------------------------------------------------------------

NEXT WEEK:
Redlands Road diversion

Redlands Road will be closed between 9th and 11th October to vehicles travelling towards Dinas Powys towards Llandough.

This is because the right hand turn will be closed to allow gas works to be carried out safely.

Details of the diversion can be found above.

As you'll see, drivers are being told to travel past the Merrie Harrier and the Barons Court to the Cardiff Bay roundabout, where they will be able to turn around and travel back towards Penarth, before using the left hand turn to access Redlands Road.

The route for vehicles travelling in the opposite direction is unaffected.

While this is unlikely to be particularly problematic for Llandough residents, I'm concerned some drivers may attempt to use the Dochdwy estate or the Merrie Harrier car park to turn around, potentially causing a bottleneck.

I've therefore put together a short video, explaining the diversion route in place, which avoids our village.

It would be helpful if you would share it on social media, Hywel.

To do so, you can click below now.
https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1CJhqM9XTD/

Road markings:
Pen-y-turnpike Road

The road markings at the junction between Pen-y-turnpike Road and Leckwith Road have now been repainted.

We secured these works together, by pressuring the Council to get them done.

It may seem like a small thing, but making it clear to drivers they need to give way will help stop accidents.

Thank you to everyone across Llandough, Leckwith and Michaelston-le-Pit who helped.
https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1EaRtbbAVJ/

Preventing overdevelopment

When I'm out and about in our community, many residents express concerns about overdevelopment and the way it threatens our village's distinct identity and character.

The proposals to build 250 houses on Eastbrook Road are a good example.

While outside our village, the site is located just down from the Merrie Harrier, on green fields that form a natural boundary between Llandough and Dinas Powys.

This boundary is crucial in ensuring both villages remain separate, unique entities.

You can watch my comments at the last Full Council meeting below.

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Fff7ZbyuK/

Dochdwy Road pavement defects

Huge thanks to the resident who got in touch about pavement defects on Dochdwy Road.

As you'll see, these have now all been marked up for repair.

By getting in touch, the resident helped ensure the issue was taken forward quickly.

When you contact me about things you spot, you're not causing a bother.

To the contrary, you're playing a crucial role in our team, as we work to improve things in our village.

That's what Our Plan for Llandough is all about!

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Hy7k64Xw5/

Community drop-in event:
20th October

Our next community drop-in event takes place at the Merrie Harrier on 20th October.

Like the last one, it'll start at 7.00pm.

The pub is a key asset to our community.

Tracey and the team do a lot for us - help return the favour by lending them your support.

You can see some of their midweek offers below!

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1EM9z5wbMs/

Our Plan for Llandough!


As your councillor, I'm working with you all to secure a better future for Llandough. Together, we have a plan to deliver for the village.

Our plan is making Llandough better by:

1. Sorting out the parking problems
2. Stamping out dog fouling
3. Repairing our roads
4. Stopping littering and flytipping
5. Delivering better sports facilities
6. Keeping the whole community involved

If you have any suggestions of what you'd like to see in Our Plan, please get in touch!

Case Ref 00210772 — Internal Review requested 7 July 2026

This is a formal chase of unanswered points already put to you. It is not a new request and must not be used to restart any clock.

On 11 September 2026 you wrote that service areas had found further historical documentation, that you were still sifting it, and that because some of it is “not necessarily Council documentation but is nonetheless in the Council’s possession” you were considering whether to consult third parties. You said you would try to give a clearer timetable by the end of the following week (i.e. by 18 September 2026).

On 30 September 2026 I asked, by Tuesday 6 October 2026, for:
1. A firm date by which the completed internal review decision will be issued;
2. A non-disclosive description of the further documentation located (date range, creator/supplier, how it came into the Council’s possession, approximate volume);
3. Confirmation that the newly located documentation is being preserved without alteration, destruction or disposal; and
4. Immediate release of any material that can properly be disclosed without awaiting third-party consultation.

None of those four points has been answered.

What you have not said
You have not identified a single document found in the September sift. You have not named any third-party consultee class, the date any consultation was sent, or the date by which a reply was required. You have not stated whether the material is held under EIR or FOIA. You have not addressed the child / personal-data point previously raised. You have not confirmed a preservation hold. Silence on each of these points is itself a recorded position.

What is now required (unchanged from the unanswered requests)
(a) Issue the internal review decision. On any view the ICO’s recommended maximum of 40 working days from the request for review (7 July 2026) has long passed. If you contend that EIR does not apply, say so expressly and identify the statutory basis for treating the request under FOIA alone.

(b) Attach a schedule of every document found in the further search: date, description, format, holding service, whether Council or third-party record in the Council’s possession, and the decision on each (disclose / part-disclose / withhold with the precise regulation or section).

(c) If any third-party consultation has occurred or is proposed, name the class of consultee, the date the consultation was sent, and the deadline set for reply. A consultee’s silence is not a ground to withhold.

(d) Confirm in writing that every document in the sift, and every related planning, enforcement, legal, committee, land, finance and correspondence record (including predecessor-authority material), is under a formal preservation hold and will not be destroyed, weeded, transferred or disposed of while 00210772 and related requests remain open.

With regards to your email of 30th September, I note that many of the queries which you have set have already been addressed in our previous correspondence. This will be more fully addressed in point 1 as I take your questions in order, below.

1) Our searches have been extensive. This has included searches of any possibly relevant registered files, the only administrative records and materials held in the long term. As I have noted, we do not appear to hold any records or correspondence in these records relating to your enquiries, or to Great House Farm more generally, including the circumstances of its demolition. Our searches have also included full searches of the NMRW archive, including both term-based and spatial searches in the archive catalogue, and a manual search for any additional, uncatalogued material. The term-based searches have included all relevant site names and related terms, as you have enumerated them. These searches have therefore included searches for all of the types of records which you have enumerated, with the exception of our historic aerial photography collections, which searches would incur a charge (see point 6, below).

2) As has been noted in my previous correspondence, no record of this correspondence or allusion to the same is extant in our records, with the exception of the brief note in Archive 6048945. For the scope of our comprehensive searches undertaken to determine this, see point 1, above.

The record is part of our NMR Site Files Collection, for details of which, please see the collection-level entry in our archive catalogue, here: https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6202405. 4) Searches of our internal records relating to these accessions numbers have revealed no further information beyond that which is available in the publicly accessible archive catalogue and noted in my email of 29th September.

Dear Adam,

Thank you for your detailed response of 29 September (RC26-0375). It is particularly helpful to have your confirmation that Archive 6048945 records Richard Suggett's visit to the site after its demolition in December 1988, and for identifying Archives 6048941, 6048942 and 6048944.

I have considered your response alongside the Commission's catalogue entries and the other records now available. Before any of the outstanding September requests are treated as concluded, I need to clarify one distinction.

You state (as in your emails of 28 May, 10 June and 11 June) that there are no letters or records concerning Tŷ Mawr Farm, Llandough, in the Commission's registered files, which you describe as the only campaign records kept in the long term.

I note that answer. My requests were not confined to registered campaign files. They concern recorded information held by the Commission relating to the site, including records which your own archive identifies as existing, lost, received or created in connection with it.

I am happy for the points below to be answered in whatever order is most convenient, provided the FOIA/EIR status and original dates of the September requests are preserved. Where a point has already been answered in full, a short confirmation that nothing further is held will suffice; I do not wish the Commission to repeat itself.

1. Scope of the search

Please confirm whether the search has extended beyond registered files to other relevant NMRW collections and systems, including (where applicable):

- Inventory working papers, drafts, record cards and historic index cards;
- field and survey notes;
- measured drawings, sketches, plans and elevations;
- maps and plan collections;
- photographic collections, negatives and indexes;
- vertical and oblique aerial photography and its indexes;
- grey literature and unpublished reports;
- special, personal or specialist collections;
- background records;
- historic administrative records;
- digital and legacy catalogue systems;
- accession and deposit records;
- transfer, withdrawal, de-accession or disposal records; and
- uncatalogued or separately catalogued material reasonably capable of containing information about the site.

Please also confirm whether the search used the principal known identifiers and variants, including:

Great House Farm; Great House; Tŷ Mawr; Ty Mawr Farm; Llandough; Llandochau; Llandough-juxta-Penarth; NPRN 20182; ST 1681 7331; ST16707335; GGAT02038s; Inventory site 425; NA/GL/88/49; NA/GL/89/208; RCS2/1/1777; RCS2/1/1776; 6048941; 6048942; 6048944; 6048945; C.N. Johns; CN Johns; and Mrs Buckler.

If any of the categories above were not searched, a simple statement to that effect is sufficient.

2. The lost C.N. Johns / Mrs Buckler correspondence

The surviving Suggett record (Archive 6048945) identifies correspondence between C.N. Johns and Mrs Buckler as having been lost from the file since 1986/87.

Your response establishes that the correspondence itself cannot now be located. Please therefore confirm whether the Commission has also searched for any residual records about that correspondence, including:

- a file cover or wrapper;
- enclosure or contents list;
- accession or receipt entry;
- issue, loan or handling record;
- reader-request record;
- catalogue or index card;
- duplicate copy;
- draft, extract or summary;
- contemporary note concerning its absence;
- later note concerning its loss;
- correspondence concerning its loss;
- transfer or return record; or
- any other record identifying when or how the correspondence ceased to be with the file.

If none of those records exists, please say so expressly. The question is no longer simply whether the correspondence survives, but whether the surviving archive contains any documentary trace of its provenance and disappearance.

3. Archive 6048945

Please provide the complete surviving contents of Archive 6048945 (every page, card, continuation sheet, annotation and enclosure).

Please also confirm whether 6048945 is a complete standalone record, part of a larger file or collection, an extract separated from a parent record, or linked in any catalogue, accession or administrative system to other records concerning Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr.

You have confirmed that Suggett visited the site after demolition. Please also confirm whether there is any surviving record giving the date or purpose of that visit beyond the description currently catalogued, or any associated site note, field sheet, photograph, sketch or correspondence.

4. NA/GL/88/49 and NA/GL/89/208

Thank you for explaining the relationship between those admission references and Archives 6048945 and 6048941.

Please confirm whether the Commission retains any admission register entry, receipt, accession sheet, contents list, file wrapper, box/listing record, catalogue amendment, transfer record or other metadata showing what was originally received under NA/GL/88/49 and NA/GL/89/208.

In particular, if 6048941 is the only surviving record received under NA/GL/89/208, please confirm whether that conclusion comes from an original admission record or simply from what is currently visible in the catalogue.

5. RCS2/1/1777 and RCS2/1/1776

I appreciate the clarification concerning Archive Numbers 6364275 and 6364276.

The separate question concerning RCS2/1/1777 remains open. Please confirm whether the contents of RCS2/1/1777 have actually been inspected (including location plan, photographs, captions and associated recording material) sufficiently to establish whether the site is Bonvilston or Llandough.

If it is Bonvilston, I will record that as resolved. If it is Llandough, please explain whether the catalogue has been or will be corrected or linked to NPRN 20182, and provide the contents and copies requested earlier.

Please also confirm whether RCS2/1/1776 has been checked for the same reason.

6. Photographs and aerial photography

I note your explanation that searching the aerial collection may involve a charge.

Before deciding whether to commission a paid search, please tell me what the Commission's existing indexes or catalogue systems establish about aerial coverage of the relevant location:

- Is there any aerial coverage containing the site?
- Is there any vertical or oblique coverage for the relevant period?
- Is there any photograph taken during or after the demolition?
- Are there catalogue entries for photographs which are no longer held?
- Does the Commission have any image connected to NPRN 20182 which is not presently visible on Coflein?

This is relevant to Suggett's statement that there was apparently no photographic record of the site. I would like to distinguish “Suggett could identify no photographic record at the time” from “the Commission has searched its photographic collections and holds no photograph of the site”. A nil return following a defined search of the photographic and aerial indexes would itself be a useful result.

7. The 1974 survey and the ownership dispute

Your quotation of Archive 6048945 now establishes (as a matter of the Commission's own file) that the house remained partially recorded because of problems created by an ownership dispute. That point is therefore settled.

Please confirm whether the Commission holds anything beyond the material already visible on Coflein concerning:

- H.J. Thomas's 26 April 1974 survey;
- the 1974 site notes;
- the 12 December 1988 additions to the plan;
- measured drawings;
- field notes;
- correspondence concerning access; or
- any decision about what could or could not be recorded because of the ownership dispute.

I am not asking the Commission to adjudicate the ownership dispute. I am seeking only to establish what recording opportunities existed and what records were actually made. (For context, the Commission's post-demolition addition to the 1974 plan on 12 December 1988 is the only institutional building-recording event identified in the immediate aftermath of the demolition.)

8. Transfers, retention and disposal

Please confirm whether any records concerning Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr were ever transferred to another repository, received from another repository, returned to a depositor, withdrawn, de-accessioned, destroyed, or otherwise removed from the Commission's custody. Where such an event occurred, please provide the recorded date, description, authority/reference and destination where held.

In particular, please confirm whether relevant material was ever transferred to or received from Cadw/Welsh Office/Welsh Government, Glamorgan Archives, The National Archives, Amgueddfa Cymru, GGAT/Heneb or another institution. (I note that the public HER entry GGAT02038s now incorporates material derived from the Commission's 1988 records; any residual administrative link or transfer record relating to that would be useful.)

9. The nineteenth-century deposit

Thank you for identifying Archives 6048942 and 6048944.

I am not asking the Commission to endorse the historical account. I would like the provenance of the RCAHMW record established, so far as it can be:

- what source was used to create Archive 6048942;
- whether that source was contemporary, retrospective or copied from another publication;
- whether RCAHMW ever examined the alleged objects itself;
- whether any accession, transfer or correspondence record connected the account with Amgueddfa Cymru; and
- whether the attribution that material was held by the National Museum of Wales appears elsewhere in the Commission's records.

If the Commission has no such provenance information, please say so. (For completeness, Amgueddfa Cymru has separately stated that it holds no record of such an acquisition; I raise the point only to establish the documentary trail within the Commission's own holdings.)

10. The demolition sequence

Your confirmation that Suggett visited after demolition makes the following question particularly important.

Please confirm whether the Commission holds any record of notification of the proposed demolition, notification during the demolition, a request for (or consideration of, or decision not to undertake) emergency recording, a site visit before, during or immediately after demolition, or contact with Cadw, GGAT, the relevant local authority, BP Properties or its agents, or Mrs Buckler or any other family member.

I am aware that the Commission may not have been under a statutory duty to receive notice merely because the building was unlisted. I am not assuming otherwise. The question is simply whether any such recorded information exists. The Commission's own addition to the plan on 12 December 1988 is the only institutional recording event so far identified in the immediate post-demolition period; any residual notes or correspondence from that visit would therefore be of particular value.

11. Search statement

Because the principal issue is now the distinction between “not in the registered files” and “not held anywhere by the Commission”, I would be grateful for a short factual search statement identifying:

- which physical record series were searched;
- which electronic/catalogue systems were searched;
- the principal names, site identifiers or reference numbers used;
- whether relevant archive staff or custodians were consulted; and
- whether any potentially relevant material was excluded because it was uncatalogued, separately indexed, deposited or otherwise outside the registered-file series.

A concise factual description is sufficient; I am not asking for an elaborate report.
